title: CERT-In AI Security Guidelines (2026): What Indian Startups & IT Companies Must Implement to Avoid Penalties
excerpt: Actionable 2026 CERT-In AI security and incident reporting checklist for Indian SaaS startups, fintechs and engineering teams covering NTP sync, log retention, prompt injection and DPDP.
html:
As Indian enterprises, startups, and fintech platforms rapidly ship LLM copilots, RAG agents, and automated APIs in 2026, AI infrastructure has become a primary attack surface. Following recent advisories highlighted in our CERT-In Crafty Falcon analysis, security teams must bridge both mandatory CERT-In cyber directives and AI-specific threat controls (prompt injection, data exfiltration, and insecure tool calls).

Mandatory Baseline: CERT-In Operational Controls Every Team Must Verify

Control RequirementWhat Indian IT / SaaS Teams Must ImplementCommon Audit Failure

180-Day Rolling Log RetentionCentralized immutable logs in India/compliant storage for AI gateways, auth & firewall eventsEphemeral container logs wiped automatically every 7 days
NTP Time SynchronizationStrict NTP sync with NIC / NPL Indian standard servers across cloud clustersTimestamp drift breaking forensic audit correlation

5 AI-Specific Threat Defenses for Production Apps

  1. Strict Output Validation & Least-Privilege Tooling: Never let an LLM run raw SQL or admin transfers directly—use bounded schemas such as OpenAI Decisions API or parameterized APIs.
  2. Zero PII Exposure to Unapproved Public Endpoints: Mask Aadhaar, PAN, UPI VPA, and customer phone records before logging or third-party cloud inference, or host sensitive models via air-gapped Ollama setups.
  3. Protect Automated CI/CD Code Pipelines: Enforce strict branch rules and secret scanning when running AI tools—read our GitHub Agentic Workflows safety guide.
  4. Website Crawler Governance: Configure proper AI training bot policies via robots.txt opt-out controls.
  5. Human-in-the-Loop Financial Approvals: Ensure payment-adjacent tools adhere strictly to NPCI authorization rules.

Detailed 6-Hour Incident Reporting & 180-Day Log Architecture

The single most overlooked operational requirement in CERT-In directives is verifiable time synchronization and tamper-evident 180-day log retention located on servers operating within Indian jurisdiction (or synchronized mirrors accessible without foreign legal delays). For startups running LLM orchestration servers or custom AI APIs, logging cannot stop at Nginx HTTP access logs—security auditors increasingly expect correlation across prompt requests, tool executions, and user identities.

  1. NTP Synchronization Verification: Point all production EC2/GCP Mumbai nodes, Kubernetes worker pools, and firewall appliances to NTP servers peered with NPL (National Physical Laboratory) India / NIC time sources.
  2. Structured AI Audit Trails: Log request timestamp, anonymized user/tenant hash, invoked tool name, safety filter trigger status, and upstream model provider ID without leaking plaintext customer OTPs or Aadhaar numbers into searchable plaintext logs.
  3. Quarterly Vulnerability Drills & Media Sanitization: Enforce strict MIME/magic-byte validation on user uploads and strip hidden metadata payloads from submitted screenshots using client-side tools such as a free browser EXIF metadata remover before ingestion into internal ticketing systems.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do CERT-In logging directions apply to small SaaS startups in India?

Yes. Service providers, intermediaries, cloud/VPS operators, and corporate bodies operating in India fall under CERT-In reporting and 180-day log retention obligations regardless of startup headcount.
